# Build handover, 2026-11-03

Milestones M0 to M4 of `docs/11-build-plan.md` are built, reviewed and merged
to `main` (merge `9279026`). The next work is the SP1 test flake, then M5. LOG 1
to 90 are approved; LOG 91 to 106, from M4, await the product owner.

| Milestone | Merged | Results note | Tests at merge (default / integration / live) |

Each results note lists what was built, the controls (deliberate breakages that
made the tests fail), the review changes and the follow-ups. Control scripts
are `tools/check_controls.py` (M1), `tools/check_m2_controls.py`,
`tools/check_m3_controls.py` and `tools/check_m4_controls.py`.

Worktrees and milestone branches are deleted, locally and on GitHub. Only
`main` remains.

## 2. How the milestones were run

1. A builder agent works on the milestone in its own git worktree and branch,
   and opens a pull request when CI is green.
2. An independent reviewer agent reviews the diff against the design and the
   approved LOG. It is given the code, not the builder's conclusions. Every
   review so far has found blocking defects, for example the model proxy
   forwarding the credential to any host in M4.
3. The builder fixes the findings. The reviewer re-checks the fixes.
4. The pull request is merged with a merge commit once CI is green.
5. New judgement calls go into `docs/LOG.md` marked unreviewed. The product
   owner approves them in chat, and approved text is never edited before then.

M0 to M2 were merged without pull requests (section 4 explains why); M3 and M4
used pull requests 1 and 2.

## 3. Open for the product owner

**LOG 91 to 106**, unreviewed. Three change approved text (marked *):

| # | Decision |
|---|---|
| 91* | New installation section `agent_worker`; `model_access` gains `upstream` and `auth`; file secrets gain `from_environment`; runtime settings `max_retries`, `hook_hold`, `client_retry`, `engine_tools` (`engine_tools: false` only with `development: true`) |
| 92 | The agent step activity lives in `Engine.Agent`, called by name `RunAgentStep`; `StepCall` and `StepOutcome` move to `Providers.Abstractions` |
| 93 | Questions are held by the workflow shell as a `question` wait, answered through the API |
| 94 | Reports are checked on the agent worker, so correction turns happen inside the session. Replaces LOG 89 for agent reports |
| 95* | No code-host credential enters the sandbox; the checkout arrives as a Git bundle. Narrower than `docs/06` section 3.13 |
| 96 | Hidden reference `refs/feature-flow/wip/<run>/<step>`, used only when it descends from the work branch; a replaced one is kept under `refs/feature-flow/superseded/...`; the branch moves only to a commit descending from its revision at the step's start |
| 97 | The work branch is created at the first agent step; `run.branch` follows `metadata.branch_pattern` (patch marker `m4-branch-pattern`) |
| 98 | Only transient model errors are resumable; 401 and 403 stop for a person; a resume is free only after progress; caps of 5 in a row and 20 in all; "engine unreachable" is decided from the worker's own records |
| 99 | How `commits`, `changed_files_unread` and `coverage_known` are counted |
| 100 | Claude Code takes hooks only from root-owned managed settings (`allowManagedHooksOnly`); repository `.claude` settings are not loaded |
| 101 | Hook policy: deny `git push`, `.git` edits, writes by a read-only role, and tools outside the role's classes |
| 102 | A cancelled step is waited for (`WaitCancellationCompleted`, behind a patch marker) |
| 103* | The provider interfaces as built add methods to `docs/06`'s signatures |
| 104 | The model proxy forwards only `POST v1/messages` and `v1/messages/count_tokens` to the upstream's own scheme, host and port |
| 105 | Each command's transcript, process id and exit code are root-owned; the sandbox client runs as the agent; step tokens are revoked at the end of the attempt; a question is shown only to the step that asked it |
| 106 | `limits.timeout` runs from the step's first attempt, kept in the record store; on expiry the attempt fails as out of time |

`docs/04`, `docs/06` and `docs/07` carry "Pending review (LOG n)" notes where
these apply. On approval, replace the notes and update `CONTRIBUTING.md` line
13 ("71 to 90 on 2026-11-02").

## 5. Next

1. **SP1 scenario flake.** `Children_ending_and_answers_arriving_during_hand_overs_are_not_lost`
   (M3's integration test of continue-as-new) failed on GitHub CI in 3 of 5
   runs after `4196ee1`; reruns and local runs passed. Two failures were check
   E2, which only confirms the scenario produced a child end during a drain.
   One was check C5, a `WorkflowTaskFailed`. That may be nondeterminism or a
   task timeout under load, and it needs the CI log to tell. The workflow code
   did not change between the last clean run (`3c8cc83`) and the failures, so
   it is probably timing. Find the cause before relaxing any check
   (`m4-results.md` follow-up 14).
2. **M5**, source control, testing and the first real ticket: the Git and
   GitHub providers, the GitHub Actions CI provider, the `scm.*`, `ci.checks`,
   `test.run` and `analysis.run` actions, and run-start checks 23 onward. Done
   when `ticket_delivery` runs on the fixture repository to a merge into a
   parent branch. Several M3 and M4 follow-ups land here: check 20 and the
   repository manifest (M3 1, M4 1), branch reset for `clean_up` (M3 5), the
   parent branch read from the code host (M4 3).

**Follow-ups that must not be lost**

- M4 12: the sandbox's network is unrestricted and `host-gateway` reaches the
  Temporal frontend. This must be fixed before any shared deployment.
- M3 10: a child run that ends without signalling never completes its
  parent's `run.child` step.
- M3 2 and 3: a child does not receive its parent's parameters, and `consumes`
  from parent, root or child is not resolved. `epic_delivery` on real
  repositories (M6) needs both.
